questions.q: Using $M^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}$, what is the inverse of $M = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$?
questions.explain: $\det M = 2 - 1 = 1$; swap $a$ and $d$, negate $b$ and $c$: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$. Inverting each entry separately does not work.

questions.q: When does a 2×2 matrix $M$ have **no** inverse?
questions.explain: $\det = 0$ squashes the plane onto a line or point; many inputs land on the same output, so there is no unique undo. A negative determinant (a flip) can still be undone.

questions.q: The **Gentle zoom** preset scales everything by 1.35. What does $M^{-1}$ do?
questions.explain: To undo a uniform zoom by 1.35 you shrink by the same factor: $M^{-1} = \frac{1}{1.35} I$.

questions.q: $|\det(M)|$ is tiny (say 0.01) but not zero. What does the page warn about?
options: The inverse exists but has huge entries, so small errors get magnified (fragile undo)
questions.explain: Because $M^{-1}$ contains $\frac{1}{\det}$, a tiny determinant blows up its entries and the condition number, so round-off errors grow on the way back.
